sentences.en: It's hard to overstate the vastness of the Skid Row neighborhood in L.A.
sentences.zh: 洛杉矶流浪汉聚居区“斯基德罗”的面积之广，怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: It spans roughly 50 blocks, which is about one-fifth of the entire downtown area of Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 它大约跨越了50个街区，约占整个洛杉矶市中心面积的五分之一。

sentences.en: In some ways, the streets of Skid Row are a bit like other parts of L.A.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，斯基德罗的街道与洛杉矶的其他地方有点相似。

sentences.en: There are corner stores and street vendors selling everything from jewelry to loose cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 这里有街角小店和街头小贩，出售从首饰到散装香烟的各种商品。

sentences.en: There are old brick townhouses filled with low-income housing.
sentences.zh: 这里有布满低收入住房的老旧砖砌联排别墅。

sentences.en: There are parks where grown-ups gather to talk, and children gather to play.
sentences.zh: 这里有成年人聚在一起聊天、儿童聚在一起玩耍的公园。

sentences.en: But it's also very clear when you've entered Skid Row.
sentences.zh: 但当你进入斯基德罗时，这种感觉也非常明显。

sentences.en: For one thing, there's the smell.
The streets of Skid Row often stink of urine and other excrement, baking under the hot Los Angeles sun.
sentences.zh: 斯基德罗的街道经常散发着尿液和其他排泄物的恶臭，在洛杉矶炽热的阳光下炙烤着。

sentences.en: The gutters are lined with trash.
And the sidewalks are mostly, and on some blocks entirely, occupied by people's makeshift homes.
sentences.zh: 人行道上几乎到处都是，在有些街区甚至完全被人们的临时住所所占据。

sentences.en: A dizzying array of tarps and tents stretch out for blocks and blocks, one structure jutting up against the next and the next.
sentences.zh: 令人眼花缭乱的防水布和帐篷绵延数个街区，一个结构紧挨着另一个。

sentences.en: And there are lots of people on the street, many of them pushing special red shopping carts.
sentences.zh: 街上有很多人，其中许多人推着特制的红色购物车。

sentences.en: The carts are handed out by a local advocacy group because the police used to arrest people for having what they believed were stolen shopping carts.
sentences.zh: 这些购物车是由当地的一个倡导组织分发的，因为警察过去常常逮捕那些拥有他们认为是偷来的购物车的人。

sentences.en: And so all a person's got to do is just be homeless and come here, you know what I'm saying, me and they register and give you a shopping cart.
sentences.zh: 所以一个人只要无家可归并来到这里，你懂我的意思吧，我和他们登记，他们就会给你一辆购物车。

sentences.en: And people usually use it to push their property around and stuff like that in.
sentences.zh: 人们通常用它来推自己的财产之类重的东西。

sentences.en: That's General Dogon walking around Skid Row with me.
sentences.zh: 那是正与我在斯基德罗四处参观的杰eneral·多贡（General Dogon）。

sentences.en: He's a community organizer and lifelong resident of the neighborhood, who's lived in both low-income housing and on the streets here.
sentences.zh: 他是该社区的社区组织者和终身居民，曾在这里的低收入住房和街头生活过。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so I was born and raised on Skid Row.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我是在斯基德罗出生并长大的。

sentences.en: They both got a job at Bullock's Department Store on 7th and Broadway.
sentences.zh: 他们都在第七街和百老汇交汇处的布洛克百货公司找到了工作。

sentences.en: They went to lunch, fell in love.
sentences.zh: 他们去吃午饭，然后坠入爱河。

sentences.en: I was born nine months later in General Hospital.
sentences.zh: 九个月后我在总医院出生。

sentences.en: And I've been downtown ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我一直呆在市中心。

sentences.en: Walking through Skid Row, it's not hard to see when you've reached the edge, the line that divides Skid Row from the rest of downtown.
sentences.zh: 走在斯基德罗，不难看出你什么时候走到了边缘，即斯基德罗与市中心其他地方的分界线。

sentences.en: And if you stand right there, you'll notice that you're at the intersection of two radically different neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 如果你就站在那里，你会发现你正处于两个截然不同的社区的交界处。

sentences.en: So, Main Street is a divider line.
sentences.zh: 所以，主街是一条分界线。

sentences.en: Main Street is a divider line between the haves and the haves-nots.
sentences.zh: 主街是富裕阶层与贫困阶层之间的分界线。

sentences.en: Because you've got homeless people that's sleeping on one side of the street and the loft building's on the other side of the street.
sentences.zh: 因为街道的一边睡着无家可归的人，而另一边则是阁楼建筑。

sentences.en: And some of the homeless people lay down in their tent and they can look up and see the TV in the loft building.
sentences.zh: 一些无家可归的人躺在帐篷里，抬头就能看到阁楼建筑里的电视。

sentences.en: So that's a divider line for your ass.
sentences.zh: 所以这对你来说就是一条分界线。

sentences.en: And in Los Angeles, that dividing line between haves and have-nots, between Skid Row and the rest of downtown, it wasn't drawn by accident.
sentences.zh: 在洛杉矶，富裕阶层与贫困阶层之间、斯基德罗与市中心其他地方之间的这条分界线并非偶然划定。

sentences.en: It's the result of a very specific plan to keep homeless people on one side and development on the other.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常具体的计划的结果，旨在将无家可归者保留在一边，而将开发项目保留在另一边。

sentences.en: It's a plan that, somewhat surprisingly, was written and fought for by advocates of Skid Row's resident population.
sentences.zh: 让人有点意外的是，这项计划是由斯基德罗常住人口的倡导者起草并为其争取而来的。

sentences.en: Back in the early 20th century, the railroad went through downtown Los Angeles, right around where Skid Row is now.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪初，铁路就穿过了洛杉矶市中心，就在现在斯基德罗附近。

sentences.en: And like many other cities around the country, a neighborhood formed around the train tracks.
sentences.zh: 就像全国许多其他城市一样，铁路线周围形成了一个社区。

sentences.en: So, first off, what do we have in front of us here?
sentences.zh: 首先，我们面前的是什么？

sentences.en: Brian Eck is a Los Angeles city planner.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩·埃克（Brian Eck）是一名洛杉矶城市规划师。

sentences.en: And the reason I brought this out is this pictorial here of 1909 actually predates zoning.
sentences.zh: 我把它拿出来的原因是，这幅1909年的画报实际上早于分区制。

sentences.en: Back when the area now known as Skid Row started to develop, Eck says there weren't any zoning laws in L.A.
sentences.zh: 埃克说，早在现在被称为斯基德罗的地区开始发展时，洛杉矶还没有任何分区法

sentences.en: to say what types of developments were allowed in different areas.
sentences.zh: 来规定不同区域允许进行何种类型的开发。

sentences.en: And so what developed at the time, you kind of had the confluence of the rail and the Los Angeles produce and agricultural markets at the same point,
sentences.zh: 因此当时发展起来的情况是，你基本上在同一点迎合了铁路以及洛杉矶农产品和农业市场的交汇，

sentences.en: which brought a large transient population in terms of the railroad workers and our agricultural workers.
sentences.zh: 这带来了大量的流动人口，包括铁路工人和我们的农业工人。

sentences.en: I've gone through the archives of the L.A.
sentences.zh: 我翻阅了《洛杉矶时报》100年前（即世纪之交左右）关于斯基德罗的档案。

sentences.en: Times' mentions of Skid Row back 100 years ago, around the turn of the century.
sentences.zh: 加里·布莱西（Gary Blasey）是加州大学洛杉矶分校的名誉教授，在70和80年代曾是斯基德罗及其周边地区的住房和流浪汉权益倡导者。

sentences.en: Gary Blasey is a UCLA emeritus professor who was a housing and homeless advocate in and around Skid Row back in the 70s and 80s.
sentences.zh: 我是在铁路调车场和市中心附近长大的，《洛杉矶时报》上把人们称为，比如说，流浪汉（bums）。

sentences.en: So I grew up around the rail yards, around downtown, and people were referred to in the L.A.
sentences.zh: 直到70年代，斯基德罗的大多数人仍然住在廉价公寓、单间公寓（SRO）或类似酒店中。
当时也有无家可归的人，但比现在少。

sentences.en: All the way up into the 70s, most people in Skid Row lived in cheap apartments or single-room occupancy hotels or SROs.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，我看到无家可归者不过是些酒鬼。

sentences.en: There were homeless people, but fewer than there are now.
sentences.zh: 再次见到杰eneral·多贡，他在70年代就住在斯基德罗。

sentences.en: What I saw when I was a kid was homelessness was just to winos.
sentences.zh: 所以你偶尔会遇到酒鬼，而且他们大多数是白人男性。

sentences.en: Again, General Dogon, who was living in Skid Row in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们过去常常喝白波特酒以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: So you had the occasional winos, and the majority of them was white males.
sentences.zh: 斯基德罗当时还不是一个后来那样庞大、紧张的城市。

sentences.en: And I mean, they used to drink white port and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然被认为是一个治安混乱的社区，人们去那里寻找毒品、整天喝酒或睡在长椅上。

sentences.en: Skid Row was not yet the sprawling, tense city that it would go on to become.
sentences.zh: 无家可归人口正在不断增长。

sentences.en: But it was still considered a rough neighborhood, where people went to seek out drugs or drink all day and sleep on benches.
sentences.zh: 随着斯基德罗的成长，洛杉矶更大的市中心地区也在发展。

sentences.en: And the homeless population was growing.
sentences.zh: 开发商们并不喜欢斯基德罗发生的事情。

sentences.en: As Skid Row grew, the greater downtown area of L.A.
sentences.zh: 例如，联合救援使团（Union Rescue Mission）就在主街上。

sentences.en: And the developers didn't like what was happening in Skid Row.
So, for example, the Union Rescue Mission, it was on Main Street.
And there were lots of people there.
It was full all the time.
sentences.zh: 第五街和主街的街角基本上算是一个露天毒品市场。

sentences.en: There were people lined up outside.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1972年出现了一个计划。
这是一个由商界人士起草并得到许多城市官员支持的计划。

sentences.en: There was essentially an open-air drug market around the corner of 5th and Main Street.
sentences.zh: 旨在将斯基德罗的人口迁出，并为更新、更富有的人开发该地区。

sentences.en: And so, a plan emerged in 1972.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“银皮书计划”（Silver Book Plan）。

sentences.en: A plan drafted by a group of business people and endorsed by many city officials.
sentences.zh: 其实质就是铲平斯基德罗。

sentences.en: To move Skid Row's population out and develop the area for newer, more moneyed residents.
It was known as the Silver Book Plan.
And it was, essentially, to raise Skid Row.

sentences.zh: 当然，斯基德罗的居民和他们的倡导者并不喜欢这个新计划。
他们开始思考如何与之抗争。
其中一人是查尔斯·埃尔瑟瑟（Charles Elsesser），当时是一名年轻的律师，

sentences.en: Of course, residents of Skid Row and their advocates didn't like this new plan.
sentences.zh: 他记得自己曾偶然看到一些研究，表明当你推倒像斯基德罗这样的社区时，

sentences.en: And they began thinking about how to fight it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着其他地方会出现更多类似斯基德罗的社区。

sentences.en: One of those people was Charles Elsesser, a young lawyer at the time,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们当时并不十分确定这是真是假。

sentences.en: who remembers coming across some research that showed that when you bulldoze a neighborhood like Skid Row,
sentences.zh: 埃尔瑟瑟承认，不管真假，这个理论都很有用。

sentences.en: it just means more Skid Row-like neighborhoods pop up elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 但为了说明这是一个错误，这是一个非常管用的理论。

sentences.en: Well, we weren't quite sure whether it was true or not.
sentences.zh: 认为如果强迫居民搬迁，斯基德罗就会在别处冒出来的这种理论，吓坏了那些不希望斯基德罗居民最终落脚他们社区的人。

sentences.en: Here's Elsesser admitting that, true or not, the theory was useful.
sentences.zh: 其中一些受惊的人加入了斯基德罗维权人士的队伍，维权人士对此表示欢迎。

sentences.en: But it was a very useful theory for purposes of saying this is a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我们确实，你知道的，想出了这个得到一些学术支持、但也极大地帮助了维权工作的想法。

sentences.en: That that whole idea was a mistake.
sentences.zh: 因此，凭借着他们仅有的一项研究，埃尔瑟瑟和其他维权人士想出了一个主意，用另一个计划来取代“银皮书计划”，

sentences.en: The theory that Skid Row would just pop up somewhere else if residents were forced to move scared people who didn't want Skid Row's residents to end up in their neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 而该计划同样会推平斯基德罗。

sentences.en: Some of these scared people joined the Skid Row activists' cause, and the activists were happy to have them.
sentences.zh: 这位是杰夫·迪特里希（Jeff Dietrich），他参与了新计划的撰写。

sentences.en: We really did, you know, come up with this idea that had some scholarly support, but also really, really helped the advocacy.
sentences.zh: 我们制定了所谓的“蓝皮书计划”（Blue Book Plan）。

sentences.en: And so, armed with their one study, Elsesser and other activists came up with an idea to replace the Silver Book Plan,
sentences.zh: 杰夫·迪特里希和他的妻子凯瑟琳·莫里斯（Catherine Morris）长期以来一直是无家可归者的倡导者。

sentences.en: which, again, would bulldoze Skid Row with another one.
sentences.zh: 他们在斯基德罗经营着一家名为“嬉皮士厨房”（Hippie Kitchen）的著名施粥所。

sentences.en: Here's Jeff Dietrich, who helped write the new plan.
sentences.zh: “蓝皮书计划”的内容是这样的：遏制斯基德罗的蔓延。

sentences.en: We developed what's called the Blue Book Plan.
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上就是所谓的遏制计划。

sentences.en: Jeff Dietrich and his wife, Catherine Morris, have been longtime advocates for the homeless.
sentences.zh: 这个新计划——我们从现在开始称之为遏制计划——提出了一些相当激进的想法，

sentences.en: They run a well-known soup kitchen in Skid Row called the Hippie Kitchen.
sentences.zh: 包括让所有的宣教所、慈善机构和其他无家可归者服务机构搬迁他们的办公地点，

sentences.en: The Blue Book Plan was this, to contain the spread of Skid Row.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就会位于新划定的斯基德罗边界之内。

sentences.en: So, it's basically what's called the containment plan.
sentences.zh: 再次听到加里·布莱西的话。

sentences.en: This new plan, we'll call it the containment plan from here on out, proposed some pretty radical ideas,
sentences.zh: 交易的内容是，所有倾向于吸引无家可归者的服务都将集中在斯普林街以东。

sentences.en: including getting all the missions and the charities and other homeless services to physically move their offices
sentences.zh: 作为交换，重建局不仅不会推翻所有的单间公寓，

sentences.en: so they'd be within the newly drawn borders of Skid Row.
sentences.zh: 还将资助一个名为SRO住房的独立非营利组织。
SRO住房信托基金将负责保护和维护斯基德罗的大量低收入住房。

sentences.en: The deal was, all the services that tend to attract homeless people will be concentrated to the east of Spring Street.
sentences.zh: 维权人士花了几个月时间撰写和制定遏制计划，

sentences.en: And in exchange for that, the Redevelopment Agency will not only not bulldoze all of the SROs,
sentences.zh: 他们通过各种途径，试图让市政府认真对待它。

sentences.en: but it will also fund a separate nonprofit called the SRO Housing.
sentences.zh: 所以，有人认识市议会里的某个人。

sentences.en: The SRO Housing Trust would be charged with protecting and maintaining a whole slew of low-income housing in Skid Row.
sentences.zh: 那是凯瑟琳·莫里斯在解释，他们找人将计划草案分发给了市议会的每个人。

sentences.en: The activists spent several months writing and developing the containment plan,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们同意趁着午休时间，把这些东西拿进来放在每个人的座位上。

sentences.en: and they worked every angle, trying to get the city to take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 于是人们回来了，市议员们回来了，坐下，拿起上面的第一件事，

sentences.en: So, someone knew someone in the city council.
sentences.zh: 开始翻阅：这是从哪儿来的？

sentences.en: That's Catherine Morris, explaining that they got someone to distribute a draft of the plan to everyone on city council.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是从哪儿来的。

sentences.en: And so, they agreed that while there was a lunch break, that they would bring these in and put them at every place.
sentences.zh: 遏制计划是一种足够的妥协，以至于不知何故，它奇迹般地胜出了。

sentences.en: So, the people came back, the council people came back in, sat down, picked up the first thing on there,
sentences.zh: 这不是一项具有法律约束力的协议，但它后来定义了这座城市几十年来对待斯基德罗的方法。

sentences.en: start paging through this, where did this come from?
sentences.zh: 而且这是一种完全独特的方法。

sentences.en: I don't know where it came from.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·埃尔瑟瑟说，没有其他人像他们那样做，而且自那以后似乎也没有人真正这样做过。

sentences.en: The containment plan was enough of a compromise that somehow, amazingly, it won out.
sentences.zh: 埃尔瑟瑟说，自70年代以来，他参与了许多旨在拯救类似斯基德罗的社区或保障性住房项目的运动。

sentences.en: It wasn't a legally binding agreement, but it went on to define the city's approach to Skid Row for decades.
sentences.zh: 但斯基德罗是他唯一一次将遏制作为战略的案例。

sentences.en: And it was a totally unique approach.
sentences.zh: 遏制计划就如何将斯基德罗类型的人口保持在社区新边界内提出了各种建议。

sentences.en: Charles Elsusser said no one else was doing what they were doing, and nobody really seems to have done it since.
sentences.zh: 计划中有一个名为“诱导措施”的部分写道：

sentences.en: Elsusser says he's worked on lots of campaigns to save Skid Row-like neighborhoods or housing projects since the 70s.
sentences.zh: 通过在斯基德罗受控区域内提供公共洗手间、长椅和令人愉悦的开放空间，

sentences.en: But Skid Row was the only time he's used containment as a strategy.
sentences.zh: 居民可能会倾向于将他们的活动限制在附近地区。

sentences.en: The containment plan made various suggestions on how to keep Skid Row types within the new borders of the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 这一部分将起到磁铁的作用，将不受欢迎的人口元素留在斯基德罗，

sentences.en: There's a section of the plan called Inducements that reads,
sentences.zh: 不是违背他们的意愿，而是出于他们自己的意愿。

sentences.en: With public restrooms, benches, and pleasant open spaces within the contained area of Skid Row,
sentences.zh: 该计划还讨论了缓冲区，它将在斯基德罗和市中心其他地区之间建立一个边界。

sentences.en: the residents might be inclined to confine their activities to the immediate area.
sentences.zh: 强有力的边缘将充当斯基德罗与中央市其他部分之间的缓冲区。

sentences.en: That section would serve as a magnet to hold undesirable population elements in Skid Row,
sentences.zh: 当斯基德罗居民进入缓冲区时，

sentences.en: not against their will, but of their own accord.
sentences.zh: 熟悉的斯基德罗环境所带来的心理安慰将不复存在。

sentences.en: And the plan talks about a buffer zone, which would create a border between Skid Row and the rest of downtown.
sentences.zh: 他会感到陌生，因而不会倾向于离开遏制区域走得太远。

sentences.en: Strong edges will act as buffers between Skid Row and the rest of Central City.
sentences.zh: 在1976年遏制政策正式通过后，

sentences.en: When the Skid Row resident enters the buffer,
the psychological comfort of the familiar Skid Row environment will be loSt.
sentences.zh: 包括许多关于如何准确遏制斯基德罗人口的细致且令人不适的建议，

sentences.en: He will feel foreign and will not be inclined to travel far from the area of containment.
After the containment policy was officially adopted in 1976,
sentences.zh: 我不记得我是怎么知道这一点的，但我确实记得学到过这个，
